claims.text: Fine-tuning T5-11B on Unnatural Instructions outperforms T0++ and Tk-Instruct across multiple benchmarks including Super-Natural Instructions, BIG-bench Hard, and LMentry.

Controlling for dataset size at 64,000 examples, T5-LM trained on Unnatural Instructions yields an 18-point gain over the Super-Natural Instructions baseline on BIG-bench Hard original task formulation.
Controlling for dataset size at 64,000 examples, T5-LM trained on Unnatural Instructions yields a 16-point gain over the Super-Natural Instructions baseline on LMentry.
Manual analysis of 200 sampled examples from the Unnatural Instructions core dataset shows that 56.5% are completely correct.
Expanding dataset format diversity via template rephrasing increases downstream performance on free-form benchmarks such as T0 Zero-Shot, BIG-bench Hard (Orig), and LMentry.
Downstream performance of models fine-tuned on Unnatural Instructions scales log-linearly with the number of generated training examples.
Using an untuned GPT-3 model to generate outputs results in severe performance degradation compared to using an instruction-tuned model like text-davinci-002.

evidence.description: Table 4 shows T5-LM fine-tuned on Unnatural Instructions (+ Instruction Paraphrases) achieving scores of 49.3 on Super-Natural Instructions, 49.0 on T0 Zero-Shot, 28.1 / 29.4 on BIG-bench Hard, and 50.7 on LMentry, outperforming T0++ and Tk-Instruct across these metrics.
Table 4 reports BIG-bench Hard (Orig) performance of 16.0 for Unnatural Instructions vs 10.2 for Super-Natural Instructions baseline at 64,000 examples.
Table 4 reports LMentry score of 42.0 for Unnatural Instructions core dataset vs 34.6 for Super-Natural Instructions baseline at 64,000 examples.

In a manual evaluation of 200 core dataset examples, 113 (56.5%) were found to be fully correct, while 4.5% had incomprehensible instructions, 17.5% had input mismatches, and 21.5% had incorrect outputs.
Adding instruction paraphrases increases scores from 45.7 to 49.0 on T0 Zero-Shot, from 16.0 to 28.1 on BIG-bench Hard (Orig), and from 42.0 to 50.7 on LMentry.
Figure 5 demonstrates a log-linear scaling curve for downstream evaluation scores across training dataset sizes ranging from 250 to 64,000 examples.
Table 5 shows that using GPT-3 for output generation drops Super-Natural Instructions validation accuracy to 4.1 ± 0.1, compared to 48.7 ± 0.3 when using text-davinci-002.

methodologies.name: Unnatural Instructions Generation Pipeline
methodologies.description: A two-step automated dataset generation framework that uses language model prompting with 15 seed examples to generate structured instruction-input pairs via nucleus sampling, followed by deterministic output generation and automated rephrasing for template expansion.
conditions: nucleus sampling p=0.99 for input generation
T5-11B model fine-tuning with batch size 16 over 3 epochs

limitations.text: Unnatural Instructions contains noisy examples where instructions, inputs, or outputs are invalid (43.5% of analyzed instances contained errors).
Generating accurate target outputs automatically requires an instruction-tuned language model, as standard un-tuned language models fail to stop appropriately and degenerate.
Automatically generated training data may inherit and reflect undesirable social biases present in the generator language model's pretraining corpus.
Human crowdworkers lack intrinsic motivation to create diverse, novel examples and frequently collapse into predictable heuristics that form annotation artifacts.
Existing instruction tuning approaches rely on extensive human annotation labor or are restricted to traditional academic benchmark distributions.

future_work.text: Developing better automatic filtering mechanisms by training classifiers on small subsets of annotated data to filter out incorrect generated instances.
Employing human-in-the-loop strategies to identify challenging patterns or collect hard adversarial failure cases to encourage the model to generate more complex task examples.
Implementing safety and bias filtering mechanisms to lower the risk of retaining biased or harmful content in automatically generated training datasets.
